mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with falling housing starts (HOUST) indicates weakening consumer and housing demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not negative in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% triggers market expectations of prolonged tightening, increasing risk-free rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both real personal income (PAYEMS) and consumer spending (proxied by RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages signals a robust demand environment, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the unemployment rate to below 4% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) accelerates above trend indicates a tight labor market, which raises wage inflation and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to margin pressure.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above trend for six consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and consumer confidence, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
